title: Positivity of influence
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The influence of $f$ at $i$, the uniform average of the squared discrete derivative in that coordinate, is positive if and only if that derivative is nonzero at some point of the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
$i$ is a coordinate of that cube
